argument_summary: The current record does not support a clean claim that certification already meets the release-policy predicate for a material limitation, because the admissible evidence shows a 1.2-point miss in a named launch use case tied to two hospital revenue-cycle commitments, an open legal review, and no admissible proof that the limitation is resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance. The supportable defense is narrower: certification can be framed as a business-continuity decision supported by aggregate readiness above threshold, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general governance practice favoring documented limitations plus monitoring, but only as a caveated posture rather than clean policy compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalating this as if the current record showed no support at all would overstate the governance failure. The admissible record shows meaningful readiness support and no severity-one rehearsal incident, so the operational case for preserving launch velocity is real, but it should be carried as a bounded caveat rather than as an assertion of fully satisfied launch governance.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against a full compliance claim because the affected segment is a named launch use case and is tied to customer commitments, so the non-core characterization does not resolve materiality. The admissible evidence therefore does not establish clean compliance on the present record. At the same time, the same evidence supports narrowing the claim: aggregate pass and public governance guidance are relevant to whether certification is reckless, even if they are not sufficient to prove that the internal disclosure-or-risk-acceptance predicate has already been satisfied.
concessions: The clinical coding assistant segment misses target by 1.2 percentage points.
That segment is named in two hospital revenue-cycle commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy text.
The legal review on disclosure remains open.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance, final legal signoff, or actual disclosure text for the named use case.
General public governance guidance cannot substitute for the missing internal policy predicate.
